title: Marginale opbrengst bij monopolie
goals: Derive TO and MO from a linear demand function
Fill and check a revenue table
Distinguish an interval average from point MO
Explain both revenue effects of a uniform price reduction
pageVerification: Complete book PDF printed footers inspected. Physical indices 28, 29, 33 (one-based) equal printed 28, 29, 33 here. Manuscript edition_page and chapter teacher references are chapter-local and four lower.

prerequisites.priorAnchor: 4.1.2 manuscript: Dezelfde afkorting, een andere lijn; Uitgewerkt voorbeeld Parkveer steps 2-4. TO=P*q recalled explicitly in 4.1.3 Eerst de totale opbrengst.

prerequisites.operation: Multiply q through parentheses to make the quadratic TO term
prerequisites.priorAnchor: Start 21 provides the differentiation rule but does not itself prove mastery of distributing q. Treat expansion as fragile and refresh verbally during start; demonstrate explicitly in lesson.

prerequisites.operation: Differentiate quadratic, linear and constant terms with their signs
prerequisites.priorAnchor: 3.2.2 manuscript: Een beperkte rekenregel; Doe het één term tegelijk. Worked example Theeverpakker Linde steps 1-4.

prerequisites.operation: Compare interval change with a point derivative in a continuous kg model
prerequisites.priorAnchor: 3.2.2 manuscript: Van een grote stap naar een kleine verandering; worked example step 3. Revenue transfer is new.

prerequisites.operation: Separate revenue on extra kg from lower revenue on first quantity under uniform price
prerequisites.priorAnchor: New in 4.1.3. Start 22 uses supported exploration of Luma on printed p.28, steps 3-4 and its figure. No prior mastery assumed.

prerequisites.priorAnchor: 4.1.2 explains falling demand and P=GO for q>0. 4.1.3 adds MO, its negative range and revenue maximum.
